memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamech, hear my words. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for injuring me. If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech seventy-seven times." - Gen 4:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the first poem in the Bible, and tragically, it is a song boasting about murder. Lamech kills a young man for merely wounding him and then brags about it to his wives. He even twists God's mercy toward Cain into a licence for his own revenge - "seventy-seven times." Pride, violence and self-glory have reached full bloom in Cain's line.

This is where a life away from God leads. It began with Cain's anger; now, generations later, killing has become something to celebrate. Sin unchecked doesn't stay still - it grows bolder, louder, more shameless with each generation.

But watch how God redeems even this number. When Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive, Jesus answered "seventy-seven times" (Matt 18:22) - the very number Lamech used for revenge. Where Lamech multiplied vengeance, Jesus calls us to multiply forgiveness. The gospel takes the arithmetic of hatred and turns it into the arithmetic of grace.

We all feel the pull to repay those who hurt us. But we belong to a different Lord and a different line - the family of God, marked not by revenge but by the endless forgiveness we ourselves have received in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you keep score of wrongs, or extend forgiveness?
- Is there someone you need to forgive "seventy-seven times"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, save me from the spirit of Lamech. Fill my heart with the endless forgiveness I have received in Christ, so I can forgive others freely.
